title: Complete Ekadashi Guide 2026
description: Dates, Significance & Sacred Stories (Vrat Katha) from the Padma Purana, Bhavishya Purana & Skanda Purana
maha_mantra: Hare Krishna Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna Hare Hare, Hare Rama Hare Rama, Rama Rama Hare Hare

ekadashis.name: Shattila Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Importance of sesame (til) donation
ekadashis.benefits: Purifies body, mind, and removes past sins
ekadashis.vrat_katha: As narrated by Lord Krishna to Yudhishthira from the Padma Purana: Once there lived a Brahmani woman who was very devoted to fasting and austerities but never gave any charity or donation to anyone. After her death, she reached the heavenly planets but found no food or water because she had never given food to anyone in her life. She returned to Lord Vishnu and asked why she was suffering. The Lord explained that although her fasting was meritorious, she had never shared food, grains, or sesame with anyone in need. Lord Vishnu then advised her to observe Shattila Ekadashi, where sesame seeds (til) are used in six ways — bathing with til, applying til paste, offering til in havan, offering til-water for ancestors, eating til, and donating til. After observing this Ekadashi properly with charity, the Brahmani was freed from her suffering and attained a place in Vaikuntha.

ekadashis.name: Jaya Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Salvation from ghostly births (Preta Yoni)
ekadashis.benefits: Grants forgiveness and liberation (moksha)
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana, as told by Lord Krishna to Yudhishthira: In the heavenly court of Lord Indra, there lived a Gandharva named Malyavan and an Apsara named Pushpavati. They were deeply in love. One day, during a performance in Indra's assembly, they became so absorbed in each other that they forgot the rhythm and melody. Indra, enraged by their negligence, cursed them both to become Pishacha (ghostly beings) and sent them to the mortal realm. The two wandered in the Himalayan forests in their ghostly forms, suffering terribly through seasons. By divine fortune, when the month of Magha arrived, they unknowingly observed a fast on the Shukla Paksha Ekadashi day. They stayed awake the entire night in the bitter cold without eating. By the merit of this unintentional Ekadashi observance, they were immediately freed from the curse and regained their celestial forms, returning to heaven.

ekadashis.name: Vijaya Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Helps achieve victory and remove obstacles
ekadashis.benefits: Promotes success, courage, and clarity
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: When Lord Rama was preparing to cross the ocean to reach Lanka and rescue Sita, He faced the vast, seemingly impassable ocean. Sage Vakdalbhya visited Lord Rama and advised Him to observe Vijaya Ekadashi to ensure victory in the battle against Ravana. The sage explained that this Ekadashi had the power to grant success even in the most impossible situations. Lord Rama, along with Lakshmana and the entire Vanara army, observed the fast with great devotion. By the divine merit of this Ekadashi, the ocean parted to allow the building of the bridge (Ram Setu), and Lord Rama ultimately achieved a decisive victory over Ravana. Since then, this Ekadashi has been known as Vijaya — the one that bestows victory.

ekadashis.name: Amalaki Ekadashi
ekadashis.deity: Lord Vishnu (worshipped through the Amla/Amalaki tree)
ekadashis.significance: Worship of Amla tree and Vishnu
ekadashis.benefits: Boosts immunity, purifies thoughts, increases longevity
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana, as narrated by Sage Vashishtha to King Mandhata: In the kingdom of Vaidisha, there ruled a righteous king named Chitrasena. All the citizens were devotees of Lord Vishnu and observed every Ekadashi with great devotion. One Phalguna Shukla Ekadashi, the entire city gathered at the temple near a sacred Amalaki tree to observe the fast. Among them was a hunter named Vasurtha, who was a sinful man. He had come to the gathering by chance and, unable to sleep due to the singing and celebrations, ended up staying awake the entire night near the Amalaki tree. He unknowingly observed the fast and vigil. When he died, because of the merit he earned from that single Ekadashi observance near the Amalaki tree, Vishnu's messengers prevailed over Yama's, and Vasurtha was taken to Vaikuntha.

ekadashis.name: Papamochani Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Frees from past sins
ekadashis.benefits: Cleanses negative karma and brings peace
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Bhavishya Purana, as told by Lord Krishna to Yudhishthira: In the Chyavana Ashram, there lived a great sage named Medhavi, the son of Sage Chyavana. He was deeply immersed in meditation. Kamadeva sent the beautiful Apsara Manjughosha to distract him. She began singing and dancing enchantingly near his meditation spot. Eventually, Sage Medhavi succumbed to her charm and they lived together for many years. When Manjughosha wanted to leave, the sage realized how much time had passed. In great anger, he cursed her to become a Pishachini. She begged for forgiveness, and the sage told her that observing Papamochani Ekadashi would free them both from their sins. Both observed this Ekadashi, and through its power, Manjughosha was freed from the curse and Medhavi regained his spiritual merit.

ekadashis.name: Kamada Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Destroys lust, anger, and jealousy; fulfills desires
ekadashis.benefits: Promotes purity and spiritual discipline
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: In the city of Ratnapura, there lived a Gandharva couple named Lalit and Lalita. One day, while performing in the court of King Pundarika, Lalit made mistakes in the melody. A serpent named Karkotaka cursed Lalit to become a fearsome demon. Lalita was heartbroken and wandered seeking help. She met Sage Shringi, who advised her to observe Kamada Ekadashi and dedicate the merit to her husband. Lalita observed the fast with complete devotion and transferred all the spiritual merit to Lalit. Instantly, the curse was broken, and Lalit regained his original handsome Gandharva form. The couple was reunited, all by the power of Kamada Ekadashi.

ekadashis.name: Varuthini Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Protection from misfortune
ekadashis.benefits: Brings stability, security, and spiritual advancement
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: King Mandhata asked Sage Dhaumya about this Ekadashi. The sage explained that Varuthini means 'shield' or 'protector' — it protects the devotee from all misfortunes and sins. He narrated the story of King Nriga, who had once mistakenly donated the same cow twice to two different Brahmins. Despite being a great donor, this single error caused him to be born as a lizard trapped in a well for thousands of years until Lord Krishna Himself freed him. Sage Dhaumya emphasized that observing Varuthini Ekadashi can prevent such karmic errors and protect devotees from the consequences of both intentional and unintentional sins.

ekadashis.name: Mohini Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: The day Lord Vishnu took Mohini avatar
ekadashis.benefits: Removes illusion, improves focus, enhances clarity of soul
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: In the city of Bhadravati, a merchant named Dhanapala had five sons. The youngest, Dhrishtabuddhi, was wicked and squandered all his wealth. His father disowned him. Penniless, he approached Sage Kaundinya, who advised him to observe Mohini Ekadashi. He explained that this Ekadashi is named after Lord Vishnu's Mohini avatar and has the power to destroy even the most accumulated sins. Dhrishtabuddhi observed the fast with true devotion. All his sins were washed away, and he was blessed with wealth, wisdom, and eventually attained liberation.

ekadashis.name: Apara Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Attains limitless merit (punya)
ekadashis.benefits: Increases wealth, removes guilt, spiritual elevation
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: Lord Krishna described the unparalleled merit of Apara Ekadashi. He narrated the story of King Mahidhvaja who ruled righteously. His evil brother Vajradhvaja killed him and buried his body beneath a Peepal tree. The soul of Mahidhvaja became a Preta (ghost). A learned sage saw the suffering ghost, performed the Apara Ekadashi vrat, and transferred its merit to the soul. King Mahidhvaja was immediately freed from his ghostly existence and ascended to Vaikuntha.

ekadashis.name: Padmini Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Observed during the extra lunar month; especially powerful
ekadashis.benefits: Removes failures, fulfills desires, enhances prosperity
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: This Ekadashi falls during Adhik Maas and carries immense spiritual merit. Lord Krishna narrated the story of King Kartavirya Arjuna (Sahastrarjuna) — the thousand-armed king and devotee of Lord Dattatreya. Despite his immense power, he committed the error of capturing Ravana and was later slain by Parashurama. The story illustrates that even the most powerful beings face consequences. Observing Padmini Ekadashi during Adhik Maas grants merit equal to thousands of Ashwamedha Yagnas — the most auspicious Ekadashi for cleansing lifetimes of accumulated karma.

ekadashis.name: Parama Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Observed during the extra month; removes obstacles
ekadashis.benefits: Removes failures, fulfills desires, enhances prosperity
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: Lord Brahma narrated its significance to Sage Narada. A pious Brahmin named Sumedha and his wife Pavitra lived in great poverty despite their devotion. Sumedha approached Sage Kaundinya, who advised them to observe Parama Ekadashi during Adhik Maas. The couple fasted, worshipped Lord Vishnu, kept vigil, and donated whatever they had. Their poverty was destroyed, they were blessed with wealth and children, and upon death, both attained Vaikuntha. The name 'Parama' means supreme — reflecting the supreme merit of this Ekadashi.

ekadashis.name: Nirjala Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: The strictest fast — observed without food or water
ekadashis.benefits: Grants the result of all 24 Ekadashis combined
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana, as told by Sage Vyasa to Bhimasena: Among the Pandavas, Bhima was known for his enormous appetite and found it impossible to fast. He approached Sage Vyasa, who told him about Nirjala Ekadashi — if one observes this single Ekadashi without even a drop of water, the merit equals all 24 Ekadashis of the year. Bhima accepted and endured the entire day and night in scorching summer heat without food or water, chanting Lord Vishnu's name. He earned the full merit of all Ekadashis. Since then, this Ekadashi is also called Bhimaseni Ekadashi or Pandava Ekadashi.

ekadashis.name: Yogini Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Eliminates sins of gossip and deceit
ekadashis.benefits: Brings social harmony and divine grace
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: In Alakapuri, a gardener named Hemamali served Kubera by bringing fresh flowers daily for Lord Shiva's worship. One day, he forgot his duty while spending time with his wife Swarnarekha. Kubera cursed him to suffer leprosy on Earth. After years of suffering, Sage Markandeya advised him to observe Yogini Ekadashi. By its power, his leprosy was cured, sins destroyed, and he regained his celestial form, reuniting with his wife in Alakapuri.

ekadashis.name: Devshayani Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Beginning of Chaturmas — Lord Vishnu's cosmic sleep
ekadashis.benefits: Ideal for vow-taking; increases patience and faith
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: After defeating the demon Shankhasura (who had stolen the Vedas) in His Hayagriva form, Lord Vishnu entered Yoga Nidra on the serpent Ananta Shesha in the cosmic ocean. This sleep begins on Ashadha Shukla Ekadashi and lasts four months (Chaturmas) until Devuthani Ekadashi. During this period, marriages and auspicious ceremonies are avoided. Devotees who observe this Ekadashi please the sleeping Lord, who grants them protection even in His slumber.

ekadashis.name: Kamika Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Removes bad karma
ekadashis.benefits: Cleanses heart, promotes compassion
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: Lord Krishna described Kamika Ekadashi as extraordinarily powerful — its merit surpasses donating land, gold, and food grains, and even surpasses the Ashwamedha Yagna. Those who offer Tulsi leaves to Lord Vishnu on this day are freed from sins of millions of lifetimes. Simply by worshipping with Tulsi, lighting a ghee lamp, and staying awake through the night, a devotee earns merit that cannot be exhausted. The Lord declared there is no better fast than Kamika Ekadashi during the sacred month of Shravana.

ekadashis.name: Shravana Putrada Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Blesses couples with progeny
ekadashis.benefits: Family harmony, protection of children
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Bhavishya Purana: King Mahijit of Mahishmati was childless. Sage Lomesh revealed that in a previous birth, the king had driven away a thirsty cow from a reservoir — this cruelty caused his childlessness. The sage advised everyone to observe Shravana Putrada Ekadashi and transfer merit to the king. They worshipped Lord Shridhar with devotion. Soon after, the queen conceived and gave birth to a radiant son who became a great ruler.

ekadashis.name: Aja Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Lord Rama observed this fast
ekadashis.benefits: Removes past life sins, grants divine joy
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: King Harishchandra, renowned for his truthfulness, lost everything due to a promise to Sage Vishwamitra — his kingdom, family, and was forced to work at a cremation ground. When his own son died and his wife couldn't pay the cremation tax, Sage Gautama appeared and advised him to observe Aja Ekadashi. By its divine power, all his karmic debts dissolved, his son was restored to life, his kingdom returned, and he eventually ascended to heaven.

ekadashis.name: Parivartini Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Lord Vishnu changes His sleeping position in Yoga Nidra
ekadashis.benefits: Promotes transformation and spiritual renewal
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: On this Ekadashi, Lord Vishnu turns sides during Yoga Nidra. The story involves King Bali and Lord Vamana. Bali had conquered three worlds. Lord Vishnu as a dwarf Brahmin asked for three paces of land. When Bali agreed, Vamana grew to cosmic form, covering Earth and heavens in two steps. Bali offered his head for the third. Pleased, Lord Vishnu became gatekeeper of Bali's palace, symbolizing His eternal bond with His devotee.

ekadashis.name: Indira Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Offers salvation to ancestors (Pitrus)
ekadashis.benefits: Brings Pitru moksha and family peace
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: King Indrasena of Mahishmati was told by Sage Narada that his deceased father was suffering in Yamaloka. Narada advised him to observe Indira Ekadashi — fasting, worshipping Lord Hrishikesha, staying awake through the night, and offering the merit to his father. By the extraordinary merit, his father was liberated from Yamaloka and ascended to Vaikuntha.

ekadashis.name: Papankusha Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Destroys accumulated sins like an Ankusha controls elephants
ekadashis.benefits: Encourages devotion and inner strength
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: Lord Krishna explained that this Ekadashi acts like an 'ankusha' (goad) on 'paap' (sin) — controlling and destroying even the mightiest sins. Even those who have committed the five great sins can be freed by observing this Ekadashi with devotion. The devotee who worships Lord Padmanabha and stays awake through the night will ride to Vaikuntha on the divine Garuda.

ekadashis.name: Rama Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Observed by Goddess Lakshmi (Rama)
ekadashis.benefits: Brings wealth, harmony, and divine happiness
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: King Muchukunda, a devotee of Lord Vishnu, lost his kingdom due to a sage's curse. Wandering in the forest, he met Sage Angira, who told him about Rama Ekadashi (named after Goddess Rama/Lakshmi). The couple observed this Ekadashi faithfully. By its merit, the curse was neutralized, the kingdom restored, and they eventually attained Vaikuntha.

ekadashis.name: Devuthani Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: Marks the end of Chaturmas — Lord Vishnu awakens
ekadashis.benefits: Awakens divine energy; marriages and auspicious events resume
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: This marks the day Lord Vishnu awakens from His four-month cosmic sleep. A pious woman observed this Ekadashi with extraordinary devotion — decorating the temple, lighting ghee lamps, and staying awake singing the Lord's praises. When Lord Vishnu awakened, He granted her liberation. This Ekadashi's merit equals all types of charity, washes away sins of Chaturmas, and opens the gates of Vaikuntha. All auspicious activities resume, and the Tulsi Vivah is performed.

ekadashis.name: Utpanna Ekadashi
ekadashis.deity: Ekadashi Devi (Yoga Maya of Lord Vishnu)
ekadashis.significance: Birth of Ekadashi Devi — the origin of all Ekadashis
ekadashis.benefits: Strengthens spiritual willpower
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana, as told by Lord Krishna to Arjuna: The demon Mura had defeated all Devas and challenged Lord Vishnu. During a great cosmic battle, Lord Vishnu rested in a cave. As Mura prepared to strike, from Lord Vishnu's body emerged a brilliant feminine form — Ekadashi Devi. She slayed the demon with a single blow. Lord Vishnu named her 'Ekadashi' and granted that whoever fasts on her day would be freed from all sins and attain Vaikuntha. Thus began the tradition of Ekadashi fasting.

ekadashis.name: Mokshada Ekadashi
ekadashis.significance: The day Lord Krishna spoke the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna
ekadashis.benefits: Grants liberation (moksha) and supreme wisdom
ekadashis.vrat_katha: From the Padma Purana: King Vaikhanasa of Champaka Nagari was troubled by dreams of his deceased father suffering in hell. Sage Parvata confirmed this and advised him to observe Mokshada Ekadashi and transfer the merit. The king, queen, and subjects observed the fast with great devotion. The father was immediately freed and ascended to Vaikuntha. Also celebrated as Gita Jayanti — the day Lord Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra.

fasting_types.description: Complete fast without food or water
One satvik meal with permitted foods

chaturmas_2026.description: Four-month period when Lord Vishnu is in Yoga Nidra. Marriages and other auspicious ceremonies are traditionally avoided.

notes.smartha_vs_vaishnava: Smartha Ekadashi follows sunrise-based calculation, while Vaishnava (ISKCON) Ekadashi requires Ekadashi tithi to be present during Brahma Muhurat. Dates may differ by one day.
notes.parana_rules: The fast must be broken the next day (Dwadashi) after sunrise and before the Dwadashi tithi ends. Specific Parana time varies by location.
